description: PULL receive path: read one page of the peer messages addressed to the calling session, on demand and without MCP. Takes the caller's own stable agent_session_id (the fleet launcher exports it as $AGENT_SESSION_ID); the agent_id and agent_instance_id whose mail is read are resolved server-side from that session's live peer_binding row, so a caller can only ever read its own inbox. Returns TWO independently paged sections. The instance section (entries, next_after_created_at) holds messages addressed to this instance and is paged by 'after', an ISO-8601 timestamp. The role section (role_entries, next_role_cursor) holds messages addressed to any role this session holds, merged across roles, and is paged by 'role_after', an opaque token. The two cursors are independent and are never mixed: passing 'after' does nothing to the role section. They also run in OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, which a caller cannot guess and must not assume away. The instance section is OLDEST-FIRST and 'after' advances FORWARD in time, so next_after_created_at is a true high-water mark: store it and the next call resumes where this one stopped. The role section is NEWEST-FIRST and 'role_after' walks BACKWARD into history, so next_role_cursor is a how-far-back-have-I-read bookmark, NOT a high-water mark; it is also minted only when a full page is returned, so at exhaustion there is no token at all. A client that wants 'what arrived since I last looked' from the role section must keep its own created_at high-water mark and walk backward until it reaches it — storing next_role_cursor across sessions instead would resume reading OLDER messages and never surface a new one. One consequence to expect in a single response: entries are oldest-first and role_entries are newest-first. role_section_status is a fault-domain flag, not a progress flag — 'ok' means the role section was computed without error and says NOTHING about whether it is drained; the role section is exhausted only when next_role_cursor is null, and 'error' means that section failed (detail in role_section_error) while the instance section was still served. 'limit' bounds entries per section, clamped 1..100, default 5: an entry carries the full message, so a large page is a large context, and the cursors — not a raised limit — are how a backlog gets drained. Reading a role message here does NOT by itself retire it for replay purposes (A4, 2026-08-04: this verb returns the full durable catch-up view unconditionally now — there is no include_important split to opt into). The surviving role-replay durability guarantee — the watcher's long-poll acknowledgement and the forwarder's confirmed emission — is what retires a role message, so a session that catches up through this verb may still see the same role messages re-served through that path until their holder acks them directly. That is expected, not a duplicate-delivery fault: treat a repeat of something already read as already handled.
embedding_description: Read the messages other agents have sent to this session, pulling them on demand instead of waiting for a notification. The catch-up read after a restart, a session clear, or a stretch with no live receiver, covering both mail sent to this session directly and mail sent to the roles it holds, one page at a time. Instance pages are complete only when instance_exhausted is true.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: recipient_agent_id and recipient_agent_instance_id (the identity resolved from the caller's session id), then two sections. entries + next_after_created_at + instance_exhausted: messages addressed to this instance, oldest-first and paged by an ISO-8601 timestamp. instance_exhausted means exhausted under the existing timestamp-only forward cursor; it does not claim equal-created_at rows were globally observed. role_entries + next_role_cursor: messages addressed to roles this session holds, paged by an opaque token; next_role_cursor null means that section is drained. role_section_status is 'ok' or 'error' and reports only whether the role section COMPUTED — 'ok' never means drained. role_section_error carries the detail when status is 'error'. Every entry carries thread_id, the sender's agent_id / agent_instance_id / session_label, and the full message (id, cursor, role, kind, content parts, created_at, action_id, artifacts, metadata).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Report the two sections separately and say whether each is drained: the instance section is drained only when instance_exhausted is true, and the role section when next_role_cursor is null. Do not infer instance completion from an empty page or next_after_created_at. Never report 'ok' as 'no more messages'. Check role_section_status before trusting an empty role section — 'error' there means the role read FAILED and its messages are unread, not that there were none, and it arrives on an otherwise successful call. Attribute each message to its sender_session_label and sender_agent_instance_id — a reply needs the instance id, not the label.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Act on the messages read; a request that arrived here is as real as one that arrived live. For instance mail, fetch pages until instance_exhausted is true before concluding the backlog is empty; for role mail, continue while next_role_cursor is non-null. Reply to a sender using the sender_agent_instance_id from the entry, and to a role by the role name.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Read-only pull of the caller's own peer inbox, plus a liveness touch on the caller's binding. Identity is resolved from the caller's stable agent_session_id via its live peer_binding row; the inbox read itself spans every peer thread targeting that identity and every role the session holds.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: A malformed 'role_after' does NOT arrive here — measured 2026-08-01. The role section has its own fault domain, so a bad role cursor comes back as a SUCCESSFUL call carrying role_section_status 'error', role_section_error with the detail, and empty role_entries, while the instance section is still served normally. Read the returned status, not just the envelope. Missing required arguments: 'agent_session_id' was omitted entirely and the registry rejected the call before the verb ran. missing_argument: 'agent_session_id' was present but empty. identity_not_registered: no live peer_binding matches that session id, so there is no inbox to read; this is the dead-watcher case. peer_session_ambiguous: more than one live binding claims that session id, which is a data fault — a session holds at most one. invalid_after: 'after' was not an ISO-8601 datetime. bridge.not_running: the messaging bridge is not active on this solet — this is NOT an empty inbox, no read happened at all. peer_inbox_rejected: the messaging service rejected the request outright; the role-cursor path does not reach it, so treat this as an unexpected service-level fault rather than a caller mistake.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: role_section_status 'error': drop 'role_after' and restart the role section from its first page rather than editing the token; the instance section in the same response is valid and should still be acted on. Missing required arguments: add 'agent_session_id' — the fleet launcher exports it as $AGENT_SESSION_ID, and peer_register, current_identity, and the watcher's armed line all echo it. missing_argument: same value, but non-empty. identity_not_registered: re-arm this session's watcher or re-register over MCP, then retry; the messages are durable and still waiting, so never report this as an empty inbox. invalid_after: pass back the previous page's next_after_created_at verbatim, or omit it for the first page. bridge.not_running: start the messaging interface, then retry. peer_session_ambiguous: report it; duplicate live bindings for one session id need operator attention, not a retry.
